cursor.exit_gate: clean — no unanswered chart claim stands against ticket 'a-node-holds-one-claim'
cursor.note: PROVED — A NODE HOLDS ONE CLAIM. A verdict no longer lands as one document; it lands as one node per criterion and one per disposition, each bare of ticket and berth framing so that identical claims from different voyages are the SAME node, with attribution riding provenance instead of content. The whole rendering survives as a pure JOIN over the parts, byte-identical to what it produced this morning (pinned by a golden literal over fixture data), so the two renderings are one function and cannot drift. THE STONE SHRANK TWICE UNDER ITS OWN CHART, BOTH TIMES CORRECTLY. The composition half died at survey: nothing in cairn/ reassembles a whole verdict from tree nodes — the only consumers are the exit gate reading the on-disk artifact and the deposit writing — so per its cast kill condition it is parts-only and the count-check refusal was never built. The token pre-flight died at measurement: the host reports prompt_eval_count ONLY in a successful body, so nothing can ask a length without doing the work. The host's own 400 IS the bound, observed live on an 11283-char whole, and it satisfies falsifier (6) more completely than a pre-flight would because no length heuristic survives anywhere — a source-scan tooth forbids one returning. THE CEILING STOPPED BEING FOLKLORE, and the reason it ever was is the finding worth keeping: inference_domain had ALWAYS recorded prompt_eval_count in its cache row, and the embed seam had always thrown it away. The number existed for weeks; it just had no return value. It does now (embed_metered_via_domain, None on a cache HIT because not-reported is not zero), and real verdict prose measures 3.71 chars/token against a 2048-token context — which is exactly why the hand-searched character boundary sat at 7403/7447. TWO THINGS THE TEETH FOUND THAT THE CHART DID NOT PREDICT. A partial landing is safe by the tree's own physics, not by bookkeeping: a mid-verdict refusal writes no deposited record, the berth stands pending, and the retry re-deposits the whole verdict where the landed parts dedupe on content hash. And cross-berth dedup fired unbidden — the drain tooth went RED because its artifact changed only its criteria, so its dispositions were literally the same nodes as an earlier tooth's. That red is the win and now has its own tooth. A1 CONFIRMED, MODESTLY AND HONESTLY: against Stone C's monolith as control, a claim-targeted query scores +0.0130 and +0.0907 higher on the matching part. One margin is slim, and a1 would have been killed without complaint had it gone the other way (validate said so before the measurement ran). What carries it is that the top-ranked part is the MATCHING claim in both cases — retrieval resolving to one claim is a capability the monolith does not have at any cosine. The standing berth cleared: the verdict that refused four times during this chart chain landed as 8 nodes; the next door read drained [] and the DEPOSIT FAILED line is gone. And the ledger now carries both record shapes side by side — a 15:48 single node_id and a 21:33 eight-id node_ids — both read correctly forever, because records of truth are read as written and never migrated in place.

window.workflow: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> [LEARNME] -> PROVED
window.note: BACK-EDGE OFF A FALSIFIED PROVED — this stone's own verdict artifact said 'a red there falsifies and rewrites this verdict', and the red came. The machinery is proven and fired correctly in anger: the PROVED crossing appended exactly one enqueued line naming verdict-20260729T121532-f211b9365e93.json, and the drain ran at all seven real door entries that followed. What failed is one layer below and predates this stone: the embed host refuses the rendering. MEASURED — nomic-embed-text carries nomic-bert.context_length=2048; a binary search over this exact content accepted 7403 chars and refused at 7447; the rendering is 11283 chars; the sibling verdict that landed earlier today was 6772 chars and is the largest node in the hypothesize tree, so this ceiling had never been touched before. Law 7 held exactly as designed across all seven entries: the enqueued line stands, pending() still derives it, the ledger is byte-unchanged at 187 bytes, every door named the failure loudly on stderr and in its payload, and every verb still served. So: criterion 3 (the loop closes in anger) FAILS on its second half, and hypothesis 5 is KILLED by its own named falsifier ('the real drain fails on the real artifact'). Bounding a rendering against an embed context is a fresh design question touching every deposit face in chart and librarian; it is not in these berths and a builder may not settle it mid-close. Kicked back to the orchestrator with the diagnostic whole.

window.entry_gate: clean — a berthed chart chain claims ticket 'a-node-holds-one-claim'
window.note: BUILDME under a complete berthed chart chain (orient 211147 -> validate 212106, the validate berth carrying the claim; buildme_rides_the_chart green by instrument). THE CHAIN CHANGED THE BUILD TWICE BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN. (1) a3 FIRED AND KILLED THE COMPOSITION HALF: measured two ways that agree — a symbol sweep across all of cairn/ and the tree's entire read surface enumerated (nearest, neighbors, tree_state, counsel) — NOTHING reassembles a whole verdict from tree nodes; the only consumers are the exit gate reading the on-disk artifact and the deposit writing. The whole never stopped being whole at its berth, so the stone shrinks to PARTS-ONLY per its own cast kill condition and the count-check refusal goes with it. (2) THE PRE-FLIGHT THE TICKET SPECIFIED IS IMPOSSIBLE: the host reports prompt_eval_count only in a SUCCESSFUL body, so nothing can ask the token length without doing the work. The honest inversion is that the host's per-part refusal IS the bound — already firing, already loud — which satisfies falsifier (6) more completely than a token pre-flight would, since no length heuristic survives at all. Also measured: no character-ceiling check exists anywhere in code; the ~7400 bound has only ever lived in an operator's hand, which is why Stone C's close needed hand-trimming.

window.workflow: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> [PROVEME] -> LEARNME -> PROVED
window.note: PROVEME with the granularity contract sealed by teeth. FOUR SEAMS MOVED, each in its own place: (1) verdict.py grew verdict_node_parts and the WHOLE became a pure JOIN over it, so the two renderings are one function and cannot drift — pinned by a golden literal over fixture data, byte-identical to 2026-07-29's rendering. Parts are BARE of ticket and berth on purpose: node_id is a content hash, so attribution baked into content would make every part unique BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the exact property that makes a monolith undedupable. Attribution rides provenance. (2) mark_deposited takes N ids; a landing that names nothing REFUSES (a deposited record is what stops pending() returning a berth). Pre-2026-07-29 single-id records still close their berths forever — pending() has only ever keyed on kind+berth, and a tooth keeps that true rather than migrating records in place (Law 7). (3) domain.resolve now returns cost+provenance additively and embed_metered_via_domain hands back the host's own prompt_eval_count beside the vector — the number was ALWAYS recorded in the row and always thrown away at the seam, which is why the embed ceiling was folklore an operator measured by eye. tokens is None on a cache HIT: not reported is not zero. (4) the deposit embeds and deposits each part separately, the content deposited being the very object embedded. NO LENGTH IS CONSULTED ANYWHERE — a source-scan tooth forbids a len() comparison in the deposit path. TWO THINGS THE TEETH MEASURED THAT THE CHART DID NOT PREDICT. A partial landing is safe by the tree's own physics, not by bookkeeping: a mid-verdict refusal leaves earlier parts landed, writes no deposited record, and the retry re-deposits the whole verdict where the landed parts dedupe on content hash — proven by forcing a refusal on part 3 of 4 and watching the retry come back duplicates-plus-two. And CROSS-BERTH DEDUP FIRED ON ITS OWN: the drain tooth went red because its artifact changed only its criteria, so its dispositions were the SAME NODES as an earlier tooth's. That red is the win — two verdicts agreeing on a claim now share it; under the monolith they differed by one clause and were two entirely distinct nodes with every agreed claim stored twice and none retrievable alone. It has its own tooth now. Suite green TWICE, and the granularity tooth goes RED against a renderer that returns the whole as one part (Law 8, self-applied). Siblings green: librarian trees, librarian loop, inference_domain, host, inspector nexus.

window.build_gate: clean — build_inspector ran 17 filters over chart
window.note: LEARNME: the voyage's learnings verified in the trees. All seven chain berths return DUPLICATE on a re-deposit with the ids they took at berth-time (orient 015b679ea9bdf7d3 through validate b4915cd9f5cd832c) — each /chart stage deposits as it berths, so the trees were already carrying them and the re-run measured that rather than adding to it. AND THE STONE CLOSED WITH THE MECHANISM IT BUILT, which validate had named as an informal seventh criterion: this voyage's own verdict artifact renders to 14282 chars — the largest any voyage has produced — and REFUSES whole at the host. As 14 parts its largest is 1595 chars / 521 tokens, 25% of nomic-embed-text's 2048-token context, and it landed as 14 nodes with 0 duplicates and no operator in the loop. Stone C's close needed hand-trimming for exactly this; this one did not.
